scope: Eight literature entries and their narrowly cited use. Published metadata and source evidence were checked without running ecological analyses.
result: Eight source identities verified. The cited scientific comparisons are supported at their stated scope. One dataset citation formatting correction is suggested.

references.title: The Copernicus Global 1/12° Oceanic and Sea Ice GLORYS12 Reanalysis
references.authors_as_cited: Lellouche JM et al. (17 authors in the published article)
references.evidence: The paper describes GLORYS12 and its physical fields. The DataCite product DOI identifies the Global Ocean Physics Reanalysis. The 202311 release and wet-cell matching are properties of the present inputs and processing, beyond what the 2021 paper establishes.

references.title: A dataset of the daily edge of each polynya in the Antarctic
references.authors_as_cited: Lin Y, Nakayama Y, Liang K, Huang Y, Chen D, Yang Q
references.evidence: The Scientific Data article recommends SIC60_6.25km_20d and specifies daily 6.25-km spatial delineations and even/odd final identifier digits for coastal/open-ocean polynyas. The version-specific DataCite deposit records 1.1.0-2023 and CC BY 4.0. The manuscript's checksum and selection operations are project provenance items.

references.title: Fast and reliable jackknife and bootstrap methods for cluster-robust inference
references.authors_as_cited: MacKinnon JG, Nielsen MØ, Webb MD
references.evidence: Wiley’s version of record gives the delete-one-cluster CV3 centred on the full estimate and discusses inference with the t(G−1) reference distribution. Defining eight informative regions in the manuscript is a project implementation choice and the source does not guarantee finite-sample coverage for it.

references.title: Effects of Sea-Ice Persistence on the Diet of Adélie Penguin (Pygoscelis adeliae) Chicks and the Trophic Differences between Chicks and Adults in the Ross Sea, Antarctica
references.authors_as_cited: Maccapan D, Careddu G, Calizza E, Sporta Caputi S, Rossi L, Costantini ML
references.evidence: The publisher article compares isotope data from four Ross Sea colonies over two breeding seasons. It links greater inferred krill contribution in chick diets to longer ice persistence and delayed summer breakup in the sampled settings, including Edmonson Point and Cape Hallett.

references.title: NOAA/NSIDC Climate Data Record of Passive Microwave Sea Ice Concentration, Version 4
references.authors_as_cited: Meier WN, Fetterer F, Windnagel AK, Stewart JS
references.venue_and_locator: National Snow and Ice Data Center, G02202, Version 4
references.evidence: The first-party NSIDC citation supplies the full author initials, G02202 version 4 and the DOI, and identifies the native 25-km grid. DataCite corroborates the DOI and title with abbreviated depositor names. The Nov–Feb average and 150-km extraction are project methods. The reference entry omits the access date called for by the NSIDC and MEPS dataset guidance.

references.title: Intraspecific variation in a dominant prey species can bias marine predator dietary estimates derived from stable isotope analysis
references.authors_as_cited: Polito MJ, Trivelpiece WZ, Reiss CS, Trivelpiece SG, Hinke JT, Patterson WP, Emslie SD
references.evidence: The published article reports size- and oceanography-associated variation in Antarctic krill isotopes and models changes in predator isotope values and inferred diet under fixed prey composition. The evidence supports the manuscript's conditional interpretation and supplies no diagnosis of mechanisms in the present data.

references.title: Using multiple-stable isotopes (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N, and δ³⁴S) to assess past and present Adélie penguin foraging grounds in the Ross Sea region, Antarctica
references.authors_as_cited: Reaves M, Powers S, Emslie SD
references.evidence: The publisher abstract and its Crossref deposit cover 15 Ross Sea-region colony locations, a latitudinal chick-bone collagen δ¹⁵N pattern, and the authors’ interpretation in terms of southern latent-heat-polynya foraging and higher fish consumption. Publisher Table S1 documents both surface records and excavated material of differing radiocarbon ages. The reported spatial comparison does not supply the positive annual polynya-area coefficient discussed in the manuscript as a non-comparable estimand.
references.access_limitations: The publisher article HTML and abstract returned HTTP 200 via direct retrieval; the publisher journal-article PDF response was a restricted login page. The publisher supplement was accessible. The alternate UNC Wilmington lab list title has different wording; the publisher and Crossref give the manuscript's current title.

references.title: Space-based monitoring of penguin diet links sea ice, food webs, and population change
references.authors_as_cited: Youngflesh C, Che-Castaldo C, Schwaller MR, Polito MJ, Serbin SP, Lynch HJ
references.evidence: The published summary and indexed methods link satellite guano reflectance and measured nitrogen isotopes to study sea ice, inferred diet and population trends. The published data availability statement cites the exact Zenodo DOI, and the DataCite record confirms CC BY 4.0. The publicly available author preprint methods independently describe 103 guano samples, five PLSR prediction components, Landsat 4/5/7 sensors and 1,000 65/35 split fits. The current optical reconstruction is a reanalysis of the source data.
references.access_limitations: The direct Elsevier full-text request and direct Zenodo file-list API request returned HTTP 403. The accessible publisher search record, Crossref, DataCite and author preprint support the checks listed. Calibration code, pixel flags, local filters and archive binary contents were outside this citation audit.

suggested_formatting_corrections: Append the verified access date and incorporate the official dataset identifier in the Meier et al. (2021) bibliography entry.
limitations: No reanalysis or new ecological claims. Source methods and ascribed scientific statements were examined only to the extent needed for the existing citations. Source pages and PDF contents were reviewed without retaining copies in the manuscript bundle.
